newsitem.title: NEPAL: Nepal Marxists table no-trust motion against Deuba.
newsitem.headline: Nepal Marxists table no-trust motion against Deuba.

text.p: Nepal's main opposition communist party moved a no-confidence motion in parliament against the 15-month-old, three-party centre-right coalition of Prime Minister Sher Bahadur Deuba on Saturday.

"If this government continues further in office the country will have to face a grave situation," former prime minister Man Mohan Adhikary, head of the communist United Marxist Leninist (UML) party told parliament. "Therefore we have initiated the process of no-confidence motion to remove it from office."
Parliament officials said the House of Representatives, the lower house of parliament, was expected to take the vote on Monday.
In September last year, Deuba's coalition replaced a UML-government barely after nine months in power.

The communists who failed to vote Deuba out through a censure motion in March this year are hoping that the Rastriya Prajatantra Party (RPP), the second largest partner in the coalition controlling 19 seats, will break away with Deuba's Nepali Congress which commands 86 members.
The communists have offered to back Lokendra Bahadur Chand, leader of the RPP's parliamentary wing who is heading the dissident group of his party, as the new prime minister if the motion is passed.
